why: Source: pick range as the volatility measure, four max-minus-min subtractions, rank (about 4 steps, with only N versus Q needing real work); question: the same range choice, four subtractions and ranking (about 4 steps), so the structure is identical.
Source: two per-day divisions, a percentage change, and the average-versus-any-month wording trap (4 steps); question: the same two divisions, percentage change and the same wording trap (4 steps).
Source: pick the right pie, sum three labelled slices, multiply by the respondent share (3 steps); question: the same pie selection, three-slice sum and multiplication (3 steps).
Source: choose the basic rate over PPP, divide income by the rate for the leading candidates, compare (about 3 steps); question: the same rate choice, divisions and comparison (about 3 steps).
Source: sum the indirect segments of five bars, ignoring totals, then apply to 2013 GDP (2 steps); question: the same indirect-only sum and percentage of GDP (2 steps).

Source: two growth rates, two projected revenues, two 2013 margins read off gridlines of an unlabelled chart, two profits, ratio (about 5 kinds of step); question: the same growth, projection, gridline reading, profit and ratio (about 5 kinds of step).

Source: value a 1% cut on the largest cost, a 1% cut on the smaller cost with its subset option, and a 1% revenue rise net of the cost that moves with it, then compare (about 4 steps); question: the same three valuations, subset reasoning and comparison (about 4 steps).

Source: see that the same respondents make the percentages addable, add four pairs of slices, pick the largest (about 3 steps); question: the same insight, four pair sums and comparison (about 3 steps).

Source: map the categories to the bars, then check four statements, two needing a group sum and share and two needing a single share against a threshold (about 5 steps); question: the same category mapping and the same four checks of the same kinds (about 5 steps).

Source: sum the revenue column, derive costs from negative margins for two statements, compare losses in two years (about 4 checks plus the cost-from-margin insight); question: the same revenue sum, cost derivations and loss comparison (the same count).
